errors.text: The orientation dependence is reversed: the target reports maximum yield stress along the <-111> family, whereas the hypothesis predicts that <110> has the higher yield stress.

The Schmid-factor explanation is internally inconsistent: an orientation producing a larger resolved shear stress at a given applied stress should generally reach a fixed CRSS at a lower macroscopic stress, not a higher one.
The sole cited evidence concerns CoNiCrFeMn nanowires and reports twinning and martensitic transformation, so it does not substantiate the bulk periodic FeNiCrMn mechanism asserted here.
